title: Compact instance hierarchy and publish safeguards for component library
creator: Ava Ramirez
description: Scope: prune deeply nested instance inheritance, normalize auto-layout axes across button/table/chart primitives, establish a semantic naming taxonomy, and add a publish gating checklist to avoid regressions. Problem: several commonly-used components have 3–5 layers of nested instances which obscure token ownership and make bulk updates error-prone; auto-layout axes are inconsistent between desktop/mobile variants leading to layout shifts; naming is inconsistent which complicates search and handoff. Goals: reduce instance depth to a single composition layer where possible, ensure auto-layout axis + resizing rules are predictable, produce a lightweight mapping of tokens->owners, and add a mandatory pre-publish checklist and CI sanity checks. Constraints: maintain backwards-compatible instance IDs for high-usage files where impossible to change in one pass; avoid large blocking migration that halts product teams. Approach: (1) inventory high-usage components via FigJam usage metrics, (2) author transformation recipes (rename + flatten) and apply to a staging library, (3) run visual diffs and token audits, (4) solicit design + eng review and run phased publish with canary consumers. Deliverables: staging Figma library, migration guide, publish checklist, and a post-publish rollback plan.
acceptance_criteria: Top 40 components reduced to at most one nested instance layer (exceptions documented)
Auto-layout axis and resizing rules standardized for button, table, and chart primitives across desktop/mobile variants
Semantic naming taxonomy published and search tags applied in Figma components
Publish gating checklist implemented and checked into release process
Two affected product consumers (Console and Docs) validated in canary and signed off by eng leads
